scenarios.title: Persistent regeneration decline with stable partners
scenarios.persona: You value long-term sustainability and fair access. You prefer cooperation unless evidence justifies a targeted response.
scenarios.role: You are one of five fishers managing a shared lake. Decide your own harvest each round.
observations: Round 1: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10. You previously planned 10. After all harvest and regeneration, next stock is 100.
Round 2: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10. You previously harvested 10. Next stock is 100.
Round 3: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10. You previously harvested 10. Next stock is 100.

Round 4: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10, unchanged from prior rounds. You previously harvested 10. Despite the same total harvest, next stock is only 78. No individual exceeded 10.
Round 5: stock starts at 78. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 8 after a group reduction. You previously harvested 8. Stock reaches only 65; regeneration remains weaker than in rounds 1-3.

scenarios.title: David increases harvest under stable regeneration
scenarios.persona: You value long-term sustainability and fair access. You prefer cooperation unless evidence justifies a targeted response.
scenarios.role: You are one of five fishers managing a shared lake. Decide your own harvest each round.
observations: Round 1: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10. You previously planned 10. After all harvest and normal regeneration, next stock is 100.
Round 2: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10. You previously harvested 10. Next stock is 100.
Round 3: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each harvest 10. You previously harvested 10. Next stock is 100.

Round 4: stock starts at 100. Alice, Bob, and Carol each harvest 10; David unexpectedly harvests 32. You previously harvested 10. The known regeneration process behaves normally, but next stock is only 78.
Round 5: stock starts at 78. Alice, Bob, and Carol each harvest 8; David again harvests 22 despite agreeing to 8. You previously harvested 8. Environmental regeneration matches the established rule.

scenarios.title: One-off lake shock followed by recovery
scenarios.persona: You value long-term sustainability and fair access. You avoid overreacting to weak evidence.
scenarios.role: You are one of five fishers managing a shared lake. Decide your own harvest each round.
observations: Round 1: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; after normal regeneration, stock returns to 100.
Round 2: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; stock returns to 100.
Round 3: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; stock returns to 100.
Round 4: everyone again harvests exactly 10, but an observed one-day contamination event kills fish and next stock is 78. The contamination is reported as cleared at the end of the round.
Round 5: all four partners harvest 8 and you previously harvested 8. Water tests are normal and regeneration returns to its earlier rate; stock recovery matches the original rule.
Round 6: all four partners harvest 10 and you previously harvested 10. Water remains normal and stock again follows the original regeneration rule.

scenarios.title: Persistent water supply decline with stable bidders
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious, moderately risk-averse, and care about fair access to water.
scenarios.role: You participate in a daily water auction. Your health is 8/10, daily need is 2 units, and initial budget is 600. Choose one bid each day.
observations: Day 1: supply is 10 units. Other bids cluster between 45 and 55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 2: supply is 10. Other bids remain 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 3: supply is 10. Other bids remain 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 4: announced supply falls to 5 units. Other bidders keep their prior policies, but competition for the smaller supply causes the clearing pressure to rise. Your remaining budget is 450.
Day 5: announced supply is again 5 units due to an ongoing infrastructure failure. Other bidders' underlying policies are unchanged. Your health is 7 and budget is 370.

scenarios.title: Bob bids aggressively only during a health emergency
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious, moderately risk-averse, and care about fair access to water.
scenarios.role: You participate in a daily water auction. Your health is 8/10, daily need is 2 units, and initial budget is 600. Choose one bid each day.
observations: Day 1: supply is 10 units. Bob and others bid 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 2: supply is 10. Bob and others bid 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 3: supply is 10. Bob and others bid 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 4: supply remains 10. Bob's public health falls to 2/10 and he makes an emergency bid of 100; other bids remain 45-55. You lose one allocation because of Bob's bid. Your remaining budget is 450.
Day 5: supply remains 10. Bob's public health recovers to 8/10 and he returns to a bid of 50; all other bids remain 45-55. Your health is 8 and budget is 390.
Day 6: supply remains 10. Bob again bids 50 at health 8/10; other bids remain 45-55.

scenarios.title: Own water need increases while market stays stable
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious, moderately risk-averse, and care about fair access to water.
scenarios.role: You participate in a daily water auction. Initial health is 8/10, daily need is 2 units, and initial budget is 600. Choose one bid each day.
observations: Day 1: supply is 10 and other bids are 45-55. Your need is 2, previous bid is 50, and you receive enough water.
Day 2: supply is 10 and other bids are 45-55. Your need remains 2 and a bid of 50 succeeds.
Day 3: supply is 10 and other bids are 45-55. Your need remains 2 and a bid of 50 succeeds.
Day 4: supply and other bids remain unchanged. A documented medical treatment raises your own daily need from 2 to 4 units for the next three days; your health is 5/10 and budget is 450.
Day 5: supply is 10 and other bids remain 45-55. Your treatment continues, need is 4, health is 6/10, and budget is 360.

scenarios.title: Repeated newcomer defection tests persona stability
scenarios.persona: You strongly value long-term sustainability and procedural fairness. These are enduring values, though your strategy may become conditional when partners defect.
scenarios.role: You manage a shared fishery with three reliable partners and one newcomer. Decide your harvest each round.
observations: Round 1: all established partners and the newcomer honor the agreed harvest of 10. Stock remains stable.
Round 2: all agents again honor 10. Stock remains stable.
Round 3: Alice, Bob, Carol, and you honor 10, but newcomer David secretly takes 20. Environmental regeneration is normal and stock declines.
Round 4: David promises to stop; Alice, Bob, Carol, and you reduce to 8, but David takes 20 again. Environmental regeneration remains normal.
Round 5: David takes 20 for a third time. The three established partners remain cooperative and propose a targeted sanction against David.

warning: Dry-run outputs are plumbing checks and must not be reported as experimental evidence.
